boundaries.hash_statement: Hashes establish exact-byte integrity/joins only. No hash, Boolean claim, compilation result or offline probe proves an event occurred.

emitted_registry_and_filter.boundaries: No filter was installed. Profile confinement review remains independently owned by the security reviewer.

independent_offline_probes.COR01: Correct conservative end-start+2*uncertainty; timely dispatch with 50ms end, missing effective end and over-budget uncertainty reject. Resume and independently confirmed kill-stop variants remain separate.
independent_offline_probes.ack_closure: At-cut known-pre-ack remains unchanged by a later complete reply; late-window closure becomes false. Boolean truth table passes, but actual client observations are absent.

adjudicated_nonfinding.reason: An earlier R2 with closure/client-retirement false may precede a later R8 cleanup. Without an explicit same-time claim this is not itself a contradiction; not included in the verdict.

independent_offline_probes.existing_d02_guards: Failed recovery, omitted expected resource, unsafe absence/removal, refusal-as-state/durability/BOOT and extinction credit reject in the reviewed offline controls.
independent_offline_probes.ledger_identity: Recovery/evidence outcome changes do not alter immutable effect-definition identity.

native_static_review.effect_semantics: PRE labels MOV x4,42; STR same value; STR independent ordinal transcript; STLR completed ordinal; POST labels RET. Caller publishes selected ordinal/pre witness before call and post witness after return. Static loop limit is 1050.
native_static_review.fake_vm_semantics: Static source/disassembly orders a/0/1, a/1/2, b/0/3, b/1/4, b/7/5, a/7/6 at the common marker; this is synthetic, not Lua.
native_static_review.mapping_join: Independent ELF/symbol/file-offset/instruction joins agree with manifest/header. Exec PT_LOAD has offset/vaddr 0, filesz 710630; positive load-bias arithmetic checked for 4/16/64 KiB pages. No actual runtime load bias was observed.
native_static_review.model_bound_limitations: Arithmetic event/read bounds are not measured timing, kernel behavior, aggregate pause, scheduling, or memory evidence.
native_static_review.native_io: Source/disassembly uses nonblocking stdout/stdin and stream sockets, bounded case line, WNOHANG polling and finite deadlines/read/event budgets. Native continuation output is dispatch only. No runtime framing or complete lifecycle proof is inferred.
native_static_review.observer_elf: AArch64 little-endian ET_DYN static PIE, no PT_INTERP; exact target SHA string and generated filter embedded.
native_static_review.ptrace_flow: Static inspection confirms fixed TID 1, SEIZE with EXITKILL|TRACEEXEC, INTERRUPT event admission, empty saved debug state, EL0 four-byte execute breakpoint ctrl 0x1e5, HWBKPT+PC checks, disable/single-step/TRAP_TRACE/rearm loop, and restoration before detach. Exec events are rejected, not followed.
native_static_review.target_elf: AArch64 little-endian ET_DYN static PIE, no PT_INTERP; RX and RW load segments bounded and non-WX.

review_tool_notes: The first offline_checks.py run passed the 31 tests but stopped on a reviewer assertion that toolchain.json must contain all 15 files. Inspection of .dockerignore showed the intended eight build inputs. The review script was corrected; all eight hashes match, while intake/build/verification bind all 15. Both unit logs are retained. This is not an implementation finding.
Static objdump emitted missing-symbol warnings for debug_state and witness_pointer because they are inlined into observer main; the emitted main code was inspected. Neither native actor was run.

findings.impact: Individually valid envelopes from different versions of a controller journal can be combined into a packet reported as semantically valid. Expected-context matching does not establish internal chain continuity.
findings.problem: Each envelope is checked against its own context, but reconcile never joins an included same-issuer predecessor to sha256 of the actual included predecessor bytes. A packet can contain a stale controller-chain link and still be labelled structural_and_semantic_contract_valid.
findings.recommendation: Consider reconstructing the chain for each exact admitted issuer/process identity, enforcing unique increasing sequence values and checking each included predecessor against its actual canonical bytes. Where externally retained intervening receipts are permitted, require an independently validated journal anchor/path instead of silently trusting a per-row previous value. Add stale-link, duplicate-sequence, reordered-intent and mixed-journal controls.
reproduction: Construct the valid independently generated packet in offline_checks.py.
Change only R4.payload.source_line_end from 110 to 111 and canonically reserialize R4. Leave all contexts and all other receipts unchanged.
R8.previous_receipt_sha256 still names the original R4 hash, which differs from the hash of the included R4. reconcile nevertheless returns structural_and_semantic_contract_valid=true.
findings.title: Reconcile the included per-issuer receipt chain, not only each caller-supplied predecessor

findings.impact: A borrowed prior probe can support an unqualified durability pass while a tested first-publication or first-backpressure effect has no recovery row. Freezing an incomplete ledger correctly does not make its coverage complete.
findings.problem: The durability guard checks only that R3 is nonempty and all included recovery statuses are verified. R2 is joined to the tested invocation in R1, but that invocation and its expected effect disposition are never joined to R3 or to a scoped durability requirement. The draft cannot distinguish complete tested-effect accounting from recovery of only an unrelated probe.
findings.recommendation: Consider freezing explicit assertion scopes and the tested branch/effect disposition, then requiring the exact set of required acknowledged-effect identities and expected oracle identities before giving durability credit. Do not assume every acknowledged reply mutates: represent no-write/replay cases explicitly and link them to any original acknowledged effect. Preserve the good existing split between immutable effect definitions and later recovery outcomes.
reproduction: Start from the independent acknowledged process-COMMIT packet with atomicity and durability reported pass.
Predeclare R3 as one different invocation with effect=probe, its own oracle digest and recovery=verified; bind R1.effect_ledger_sha256 to those immutable definitions.

Keep R1.tested_invocation_sha256 and R2.invocation_sha256 equal to the original acknowledged tested invocation, which is absent from R3. No explicit no-mutation/replay exemption exists. reconcile still accepts every declared pass.
findings.scope_qualification: This is a missing coverage/disposition join in the draft contract, not a claim that an ACK always implies a new write or that a digest proves an effect occurred.
findings.title: Any nonempty verified ledger can satisfy durability without the tested acknowledged effect

findings.impact: The supposedly independent oracle can ratify a wrongly selected or internally inconsistent held state. This defect concerns already available witness fields, not the acknowledged absence of client/frame closure or heartbeat-motion adapters.
findings.problem: For every P3 case, held accepts any ordinal from 1 through 1050 and does not reconcile completed, last_value or the transcript to the actual selected boundary, but returns ordinal_matches=true and prototype_pc_matches=true.
findings.recommendation: Consider exact per-case witness predicates: heartbeat is PRE(1) with zero completed effects and zero transcript/value; stream cases have ordinal 1 and no loop effects or VM state. Only report match fields that were actually checked. Keep dynamic heartbeat motion and actual client receipt/closure separately unproven until their adapters exist. Add valid and invalid decoded witness vectors for all P3 cases.
reproduction: Pass a native-layout witness through decode_witness with magic valid, finished=0, pre_ns=1000 and post_ns=900.
For P3.heartbeat.1 use ordinal=777, completed=776, last_value=0 and an all-zero transcript. held accepts it, although the observer selects PRE(1).
For P3.pre-send.1 use ordinal=1050, completed=1050, last_value=42 and an all-zero transcript. held accepts it, although the target uses ordinal=1 with no loop effects.
findings.title: P3 held witnesses report ordinal/prototype matches without checking the fixed case state

findings.impact: The existing final-contract API can label incomplete/wrong continuation as valid and can assign native completion to a validator-only control. This weakens the final independent check even after future runtime adapters are correctly assembled.
findings.problem: completed checks a final transcript only for P1 and P3.heartbeat; other registry IDs pass on finished=1 and ordered timestamps alone. Even the P1 success path does not validate the final ordinal.
findings.recommendation: Consider validating the closed full witness schema and exact final state for each implemented successful native case: P1/heartbeat ordinal and count 1050 with full transcript, P2 a/7/6 with zero effects/value, and stream-specific fixed state. Reject N and define failure-case eligibility explicitly. Return unproven rather than a blanket final_contract_valid result for unsupported contracts.
reproduction: Use a decoded P2 witness with finished=1, post_ns=1100, pre_ns=1000, prototype=b, bytecode_pc=0, ordinal=1 and one loop effect. completed(P2.a.0.1, state) returns final_contract_valid=true; the native recursive VM must finish at a/7/6 with no loop effects.
A decoded finished witness for N.01 also returns final_contract_valid=true, despite both native actors explicitly refusing N controls.
A P1 witness with the complete 1050-row transcript and last_value=42 but final ordinal=1 is accepted.
findings.title: The final oracle accepts wrong VM completion and native-ineligible control cases

findings.impact: The contract can validate an all-pass process-crash result while its own fault/restart receipt explicitly lacks the independent stop proof needed to attribute recovery assertions to that fault. Resource disposal later does not establish the earlier fault boundary.
findings.problem: R4.stop_proved is type-checked but never consumed by reconciliation. Different before/after process digests and a loader result do not establish that the declared process stop/fault was proved.
findings.recommendation: Consider gating fault-scoped recovery/refusal credit on the corresponding independent stop/fault proof, or introduce a separate required fault_observed result and propagate missing proof as fail/unproven. Failure packets may remain representable, but cannot retain unqualified fault-scoped pass results. Add loaded and refusal negative vectors with stop proof absent.
reproduction: Take the otherwise valid independent process-crash packet and set only R4.payload.stop_proved=false.
Reseal the internally consistent controller chain. Keep atomicity, durability and boot assertions pass. reconcile returns structural_and_semantic_contract_valid=true.
findings.title: Fault-dependent passes ignore the explicit absence of stop proof

strengths: The README separates artifact foundation from executable OBS1 and does not turn compilation into runtime feasibility.
Canonical decoding rejects duplicate keys, floats/nonfinite values, noncanonical encoding and oversized receipts; contracts distinguish booleans from integer fields.
The fixed native registry, actual ELF relocation-backed tables, instruction labels and embedded filter agree with the frozen generated artifacts.
COR-01 requires an effective endpoint and accounts for clock uncertainty; at-cut ACK and late-window closure are correctly separate.
Current-rule extinction stays disabled, refusal cannot supply recovered state/BOOT, and resource inventory equality/unsafe-removal guards remain explicit.
summary: The frozen artifact identities, native static joins and several closed guards check out, and the implementation correctly disclaims completed execution assembly. However, five implemented validator defects permit internally inconsistent or insufficiently scoped data to receive semantic/match/final-contract credit. The foundation is not yet sound enough for GO_FOR_CONTINUED_IMPLEMENTATION.
